paragraphs: One-line judgment: Automotive Engineers are not "technician-level test execution" but use computer-aided design technology to develop new or improved designs for vehicle structural members, engines, transmissions, or other vehicle systems and direct the building, modification, or testing of vehicles or components: validating performance and safety through system-level tests, performing failure, variation, and root cause analysis, calibrating vehicle systems including control algorithms, and developing engineering specifications and quality control standards; people who only want ready-made solutions and are unwilling to take responsibility for design assumptions and the basis of validation are not suited to it.

Signals to keep exploring: you can read drawings, standards, and specifications, are willing to use engineering analysis (mechanics, thermal science, electronics, and control) to turn requirements into verifiable design solutions, are willing to check performance and safety metrics against test and calibration methods, and can stop and verify when the basis is unclear, test conditions are not met, or compliance requirements change.

Conditions for pausing your investment: you have not yet completed one full design—analysis—test—review loop under any supervised conditions, or you can only describe your interest as "liking cars"; also do not treat course grades or proficiency with a software product as proof that you can independently sign design conclusions, calibration parameters, or compliance determinations. Design decisions involving vehicle safety, emissions, and new energy systems must be made per the applicable standards and institutional processes and must leave a traceable basis; this page does not provide design, test, or field work instructions.

Education and authorization must be verified separately: O*NET lists 17-2141.02 as Job Zone Four (SVP 7.0 to <8.0), and among the education levels published on the page 71% is requiring a bachelor's degree, 14% is requiring a master's degree, and 5% is requiring a postsecondary certificate; the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook lists the typical entry-level education for this occupation family as a bachelor's degree, with no related work experience and no on-the-job training required, and also notes that every U.S. state and the District of Columbia requires mechanical engineers who offer services to the public to be licensed. On the mainland China side, "automotive engineer" is not listed separately in the Occupational Classification Code (2022 edition), and the position falls under the engineering technician intermediate class, with specific position requirements set by the employer and industry rules. Education, engineering program accreditation, professional licensure (PE), institutional design review authorization, and product market access approval are different statuses and must be verified item by item according to employer, position, and location.

One line: this is an engineering position that turns requirements into verifiable designs and takes responsibility for design assumptions; the core is design and development, analysis and validation, calibration and testing, failure and root cause analysis, specification and quality standard development, and cross-functional collaboration, rather than an interest in cars or proficiency with a software product.

The work of Automotive Engineers falls into three categories: design and development (designing or analyzing vehicle systems with computer-aided design technology, covering fields such as aerodynamics, alternative fuels, ergonomics, hybrid power, brakes, transmissions, steering, calibration, safety, or diagnostics; developing new or improved designs for vehicle structural members, engines, transmissions, or other vehicle systems; creating alternative design options for vehicle components, such as camless or dual-clutch engines or alternative air conditioning systems, to improve fuel efficiency; designing vehicles that use lightweight materials such as aluminum, magnesium alloys, or plastics; designing vehicles that improve recyclability or use natural, renewable, or recycled materials; and developing specifications for vehicles using alternative fuels or alternative power); testing, calibration, and analysis (conducting or directing system-level automotive testing, performing failure, variation, or root cause analysis, calibrating vehicle systems including control algorithms or other software systems, developing calibration methods, test methods, or tools, building models for algorithm or control function validation testing, designing control systems or algorithms for energy management, emissions management, or improved operating safety or performance, and researching or implementing green automotive technology involving alternative fuels and electric or hybrid power); and specifications, review, and collaboration (developing engineering specifications or cost estimates for automotive design concepts, establishing production or quality control standards, modifying designs to achieve specified function or operating performance, conducting automotive design reviews, writing and reviewing and maintaining engineering documentation, preparing or presenting technical and project status reports, coordinating production activities with other functions such as procurement, maintenance, or quality control, and providing technical guidance to other engineers or engineering support personnel). All three categories presuppose stopping and escalating when the design assumptions, test conditions, or compliance basis are unclear.

O*NET occupational identity and tasks: O*NET 17-2141.02 Automotive Engineers (page updated in 2026); this code is a detailed occupation under 17-2141 Mechanical Engineers. The official duties are to use computer-aided design technology to develop new or improved designs for vehicle structural members, engines, transmissions, or other vehicle systems and to direct the building, modification, or testing of vehicles or components; there are 25 official tasks, of which the highest importance ratings are conducting or directing system-level automotive testing (81), providing technical guidance to other engineers or engineering support personnel, performing failure, variation, and root cause analysis (80), calibrating vehicle systems including control algorithms or other software systems (79), and designing or analyzing automotive systems in fields such as aerodynamics, alternative fuels, ergonomics, hybrid power, brakes, transmissions, steering, calibration, safety, or diagnostics (71), followed by writing or presenting technical and project status reports (70), conducting research to develop new concepts (69), establishing production or quality control standards (69), and modifying designs to achieve specified performance (69). The task list describes the work of the group as a whole and does not mean every job performs all tasks. All details25 tasks are Core, with Importance81 system testing 81 / technical guidance 81 / failure and variation root cause 80 / calibration 79 / system design 71, and the activities details list 41 items, led by computers 93, decision making 89, analysis 86, getting information 86, and evaluating compliance 83; the scores are not frequency or an individual threshold. The computerized automotive application research mentions AI, telematics, and ITS, which is not a measurement that generative AI has been adopted or has improved efficiency in this occupation.

entries: Requirements and constraints | Make the goals measurable | Collect functional, performance, regulatory, and cost constraints, turn the requirements into verifiable design goals and acceptance criteria, and mark the steps that need review and authorization.

Design and analysis | Make the solution verifiable | Use computer-aided design to build and analyze vehicle system solutions, create alternatives and compare trade-offs, and record assumptions, models, and versions.

Testing and calibration | Make the conclusions reviewable | Conduct or direct system-level testing, calibrate vehicle systems including control algorithms, collect and analyze data against the acceptance criteria, and describe anomalies and deviations.

Failure and root cause | Make the problem locatable | Perform failure, variation, or root cause analysis, distinguish symptoms from causes, and record the basis for determinations and the reproduction conditions.

Specifications and standards | Make the deliverables executable | Develop engineering specifications and cost estimates and production or quality control standards, write and review and maintain engineering documentation, conduct design reviews, and track changes.

Collaboration and guidance | Make responsibility attributable | Coordinate with functions such as procurement, manufacturing, and quality control, provide technical guidance to other engineers or engineering support personnel, and handle product market access and compliance determinations through qualified and authorized organizations and processes.

paragraphs:
Work environment | 100% use email every day, 75% need face-to-face discussions every day, 70% talk on the telephone every day, 70% work indoors in a controlled environment every day, 90% have a regular work schedule, and 14% wear routine protective or safety equipment every day.
Main equipment and systems | Computer-aided design (AutoCAD, CATIA, SolidWorks, and so on) and engineering analysis software (MATLAB, Simulink, Minitab, and so on), test benches and data acquisition systems, calibration and diagnostic tools, and prototype vehicles and test specimens.
Task rhythm | 71% work more than 40 hours per week, 19% face time pressure every day, 48% face time pressure at least once a week but not every day, 57% sit more than half the time, 70% stand less than half the time, and 84% walk or run less than half the time.
Collaboration | Work with design engineers and engineering support personnel, the test and calibration team, and functions such as procurement, manufacturing, and quality control; 70% consider cooperation with the work team extremely important, 24% have continuous contact with others, and for coordinating or leading others (the item explicitly excludes supervisors or team leads): 45% consider it very important and 20% extremely important, so this cannot be taken as 65% holding leadership roles.
Competition and pressure | 43% consider competition intense and 38% consider it moderate; 33% consider the consequences of errors extremely serious and 43% fairly serious; 38% consider their decisions to have an important effect on colleague or company results; 20% carry very high responsibility for the health and safety of others and 35% carry high responsibility.
Compliance and safety | Mainland China's new energy vehicle market access rules apply to domestic manufacturers and their products for use in China: manufacturers must have the required production, conformity, after-sales, and safety capabilities; products must meet the special and general standards and safety conditions and be tested by a nationally recognized testing agency, with technical review and announcement handled by the specified body and MIIT. This is not an individual engineer's license or training certificate. The 2026 No. 1 market access review requirements announcement takes effect 2027-01-01 and must not be claimed as already implemented, and the complete annex conditions were not read. GB7258-2017 official platform status is current (including Amendment No. 2); GB7258-2026 was released 2026-08-27 and takes effect 2027-07-01, so its current status is about to be implemented. The door, emergency rescue, and battery monitoring items proposed in the old 20250058-Q-312 revision project are only revision notes and cannot be treated as current or final articles. This round obtained only the status metadata of the two versions, not the final full standard text or the complete transition conditions, and no field work is authorized on the basis of the project description. The EPA vehicle testing regulations page is a regulatory overview and link index, stating that manufacturers test per the applicable CFR test procedures, with 1066 and 86 applying by vehicle class and model year; the 86B condition through model year 2021 alone cannot be taken as the current uniform requirement for all vehicles. This round did not read all CFR and vehicle certification procedures, and this is not individual engineer certification or a complete field operating rule.
Records and review | Requirements, design assumptions, analysis methods and versions, and test and calibration conditions and conclusions need to be traceable; 48% consider precision or accuracy extremely important (and another 48% consider it very important), 38% have a lot of freedom to decide tasks, priorities, and goals, 14% make decisions every day (24% weekly but not daily), and 14% consider repeating the same task extremely important.
Skills and training | O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone Four (SVP 7.0 to <8.0); the basic skills rank critical thinking (78) and reading comprehension (75) highest, the cross-functional skills include complex problem solving, judgment and decision making, operations analysis, systems analysis, and systems evaluation; knowledge is mainly engineering and technology, physics, mathematics, mechanical, and design; the abilities rank deductive reasoning, inductive reasoning, oral comprehension, oral expression, and problem sensitivity highest.
Education and training supplement | The O*NET new-hire education survey: 71% bachelor's, 14% master's, and 5% postsecondary certificate, which is the respondent proportion for the education new hires need, not the incumbent composition, the same survey at the parent level, or a uniform threshold. Zone4/SVP7 to <8 describes a zone generally requiring considerable skills, knowledge, and experience, with most requiring a four-year bachelor's degree but with exceptions, and usually several years of related experience and on-the-job or career training, which is not a fixed number of years for all positions in this occupation. The BLS parent-level typical bachelor's degree (mechanical engineering or mechanical engineering technology) with experience None/OJT None is a statistical classification, not a requirement of no experience or a ban on training.
Entry and authorization | BLS parent-level OOH: entry-level mechanical engineer positions do not require licensure, and all states and DC require a license for mechanical engineers who sell engineering services to the public; a PE may supervise, seal projects, and serve the public. Common requirements are an accredited education, the FE, related experience (usually at least 4 years), and the PE examination, with specific states and alternative pathways to be verified separately; passing the FE is only the EIT/EI pathway and does not equal a PE or product market access decision authority. China's special operations training and assessment provisions take effect 2026-06-01, and the corresponding training, assessment, and certification are verified by catalog and actual task; an internal authorization or supervision cannot replace the statutory conditions; the catalog was not fully verified, and the same electrical work certificate is not required of all automotive engineers. U.S. OSHA1910.333 electrical work in principle requires de-energizing first, and energized exceptions require the article's conditions and qualified personnel; lockout/tagout and voltage verification follow the real procedures. 1910.147 covers unexpected startup or stored energy hazards during servicing and maintenance and does not apply wholesale to ordinary production operations, and electrical utilization equipment hazards are distinguished under Subpart S. The relevant applicable parts and a—c parts that were read are not all fuel, fire, and environmental or stop and recovery procedures.
Industry and employers | The current O*NET broad industry data is taken from the parent 17-2141: manufacturing 44%, professional, scientific, and technical services 32%, and other 24%, which is not an automotive detailed occupation or Chinese distribution. The OOH detailed industry employment is architectural and engineering related services 20%, machinery manufacturing 14%, transportation equipment manufacturing 10%, scientific research and development 7%, and computer and electronic product manufacturing 6%, at a different classification level. Vehicle and parts manufacturing, test and calibration, and consulting serve as editorial comparison directions, and no real recruiting was read.
Design and development tasks

U.S. wage distribution (under the same family 17-2141.00 definition): the 2025 BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS) shown by O*NET give, for 17-2141.00 Mechanical Engineers, annual wages of $73,990 at the 10th percentile, $84,130 at the 25th percentile, $104,110 at the median, $132,590 at the 75th percentile, and $164,340 at the 90th percentile; hourly wages are $35.57 at the 10th percentile, $40.45 at the 25th percentile, $50.05 at the median, $63.75 at the 75th percentile, and $79.01 at the 90th percentile. The BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook gives a 2025 median annual wage of $104,110 (median hourly wage $50.05) for the same occupation family. The O*NET page explicitly states that the wage data for this detailed occupation is taken from the occupation family, so this page does not treat it as an independent statistic for the detailed occupation; the median is not an entry-level wage and does not constitute an income promise. OEWS paid employee wages include base pay, commissions, production bonuses, and other incentive pay and tips, and exclude overtime premiums, shift differentials, and nonproduction bonuses; they cannot be entirely excluded on the basis of a project or performance label. The self-employed, owners and partners of unincorporated businesses, and unpaid family workers are excluded, and paid corporate employees are not all excluded on the basis of a consultant or family business label; this is not an individual's total take-home income.

Collect requirements and constraints → build concept solutions and alternatives → engineering analysis and simulation → develop specifications and cost estimates → design review and modification → deliver a verifiable design solution.

Mainland China side: the National Bureau of Statistics' Average Annual Wages of Urban Employed Persons in 2025 (released 2026-05-15) shows 129,441 yuan/year for urban non-private units nationwide, 71,590 yuan/year for urban private units, and 106,080 yuan/year for enterprises above designated size; the industry category closest to this occupation is manufacturing (non-private 113,594 yuan/year, private 76,055 yuan/year); the comparison job categories are professional and technical personnel in enterprises above designated size at 155,491 yuan/year, office and related personnel at 94,936 yuan/year, and middle-level and above managers at 210,016 yuan/year. Under the evidence definitions of this page, the industry category and job category figures above are shown separately as an industry proxy and a job category proxy, are not combined into a salary range, and are not treated as the occupational income of automotive engineers. The NBS total wage may, by the nature of the payments, include bonuses, performance pay, piece rates, allowances and subsidies, and overtime pay, and project bonuses and annual performance pay cannot all be excluded; excluded items are verified separately per the rules. Industry and job category averages are not the wage of automotive engineers.
Testing and validation tasks

U.S. parent level 17-2141 mechanical engineers: 298,500 jobs in 2025, projected at 332,000 in 2035, growing 11.2% (OOH/O*NET rounded to 11%, much faster than average), a net gain of 33,500, about 17,800 openings per year, and 0.5% self-employed. This is not an independent statistic for 17-2141.02 Automotive Engineers; openings include growth and replacements and are not the net gain, an individual hiring rate, or generative AI causality.

Determine the validation goals and acceptance criteria → conduct or direct system-level testing → collect and analyze data → perform failure and root cause analysis → calibrate systems and algorithms → form reviewable conclusions and a statement of limitations.

The current O*NET broad industry data is taken from the parent 17-2141: manufacturing 44%, professional, scientific, and technical services 32%, and other 24%, which is not an automotive detailed occupation or Chinese distribution. The OOH detailed industry employment is architectural and engineering related services 20%, machinery manufacturing 14%, transportation equipment manufacturing 10%, scientific research and development 7%, and computer and electronic product manufacturing 6%, at a different classification level. In 2025 the only job-posting hot technologies linked to this U.S. occupation were 36 items, with the proportion being the number of unique postings mentioning the skill divided by all unique postings linked to the occupation: AutoCAD13%, Office13%, Excel11%, PowerPoint8%, Python8%, SolidWorks7%, MATLAB6%, Outlook4%, C++3%, Word2%, C2%, and SQL/Perl/Jenkins/JIRA/Salesforce/Linux/Git each 1%; C#/SAP/Visio/Project are below 1%, and the other 14 items are at a proportion of Not available and cannot be filled in as zero. The 7 In Demand marks in the hot list do not equal the 10 In Demand skills in the summary, and the label means the skill is commonly listed in postings and does not prove a labor shortage, the adoption rate of incumbents, or a threshold for all positions.

Work with design engineers and engineering support personnel, the test and calibration team, functions such as procurement, manufacturing, and quality control, and suppliers and external testing and certification organizations; when vehicle safety, emissions, functional safety, new energy high-voltage systems, and data and intellectual property are involved, follow the applicable standards and institutional procedures, do not decide on your own, and stop and escalate when the basis is unclear.

Automotive Engineers focus on the design, development, and validation of vehicles and vehicle systems and take responsibility for design assumptions and the basis of validation; mechanical engineers (same family 17-2141.00) focus on the design and development of broader mechanical and thermal systems; automotive engineering technicians focus on test preparation and execution and data collection and usually do not carry design sealing responsibility; fuel cell engineers (same SOC 17-2141.01) focus on fuel cell systems; aerospace engineers focus on aircraft and systems; electrical engineers focus on electrical systems and equipment; industrial engineers focus on process and efficiency optimization; validation engineers focus on validation strategy and compliance conclusions. Adjacent occupations share mathematics, physics, and engineering fundamentals, but the objects, deliverables, and responsibilities differ.
Verifiable, reviewable design and validation conclusions

Turn requirements into a verifiable design solution and validation conclusions, and leave engineering documentation stating the design assumptions and constraints, analysis methods and models, test and calibration conditions, results and failure analysis, conclusions and limitations, and open items, so that reviewers or the lead engineer can judge from it.
Design documents and validation reports

The objects are whole vehicles and vehicle systems (structural members, engines, transmissions, brakes, steering, suspension, electrical and electronic control systems, energy management and emissions control systems, and alternative fuel and alternative power systems); the basis is national and industry standards, engineering specifications and test and calibration methods, functional safety and emissions and safety regulatory requirements, and the institution's design review and change control processes.

Automotive Engineers (U.S. side O*NET 17-2141.02, Automotive Engineers; this code is a detailed occupation under 17-2141 Mechanical Engineers) use computer-aided design technology to develop new or improved designs for vehicle structural members, engines, transmissions, or other vehicle systems, and they direct the building, modification, or testing of vehicles or components. The original official duties read "Develop new or improved designs for vehicle structural members, engines, transmissions, or other vehicle systems, using computer-assisted design technology. Direct building, modification, or testing of vehicle or components."; O*NET lists 25 official tasks, focused on conducting or directing system-level automotive testing, providing technical guidance to other engineers or engineering support personnel, performing failure, variation, or root cause analysis, calibrating vehicle systems including control algorithms or other software systems, designing or analyzing automotive systems involving aerodynamics, alternative fuels, ergonomics, hybrid power, brakes, transmissions, steering, calibration, safety, and diagnostics, writing or presenting technical and project status reports, conducting research to develop new concepts in automotive engineering, establishing production or quality control standards, modifying designs to achieve specified performance, researching or implementing green automotive technology, developing calibration methods or test methods or tools, creating alternative design options for vehicle components to improve fuel efficiency, developing or implementing operating methods or processes, developing engineering specifications or cost estimates for automotive design concepts, conducting automotive design reviews, designing vehicles using lightweight materials, writing and reviewing and maintaining engineering documentation, developing specifications for vehicles using alternative fuels or alternative power, building models for algorithm or control function validation testing, coordinating production activities with other functions such as procurement, maintenance, and quality control, designing control systems or algorithms for energy management or emissions management or improved operating safety or performance, developing or integrating control function requirements, researching computerized automotive applications such as long-range telematics, intelligent transportation systems, artificial intelligence, and automatic controls, tracking new automotive technology and competing products, and designing vehicles that improve recyclability or use natural, renewable, and recycled materials. In the United States this occupation is in Job Zone Four (SVP 7.0 to <8.0); mainland China statistics are aggregated by industry category and job category and do not list this occupation separately. This page does not constitute design, test, or field work instructions, and the relevant decisions must be made by organizations and personnel with the appropriate qualifications and authorization following the applicable standards and processes.
Requirements—design—analysis—test—calibration—review

Confirm the requirements and regulatory constraints → build and analyze the design solution → conduct testing and calibration against the acceptance criteria → perform failure and root cause analysis → modify the design and review → form conclusions and a statement of limitations.
Reviewable design and validation documentation

Requirements and constraints, design assumptions and alternatives, analysis methods and models and versions, test and calibration conditions, data and processing steps, failure analysis conclusions, design change and review records, and the parts that remain uncertain.
The individual and the lead engineer (or the design review and quality department)

The accuracy of design assumptions, analysis methods, and test and calibration conclusions is the individual's responsibility; product market access, type approval, and compliance determinations are made by organizations and personnel with the appropriate qualifications and authorization, and when the basis is unclear or the work is beyond the authorized scope, work must stop and be escalated.
Education and preparation

O*NET lists 17-2141.02 as Job Zone Four (SVP 7.0 to <8.0), typically requiring a four-year bachelor's degree and considerable related work skills, knowledge, or experience; among the education levels published on the page, 71% is requiring a bachelor's degree, 14% is requiring a master's degree, and 5% is requiring a postsecondary certificate. The BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook lists the typical entry-level education for this occupation family as a bachelor's degree (mechanical engineering or mechanical engineering technology), with no related work experience and no on-the-job training required. O*NET also lists 36 hot technologies (including Autodesk AutoCAD 13%, Microsoft Office 13%, Excel 11%, PowerPoint 8%, Python 8%, SolidWorks 7%, and MATLAB 6%, given by the page as the proportion of appearance in employer job postings). On the mainland China side, training is mainly in majors such as vehicle engineering and mechanical engineering and automation, with specific requirements set by the employer.
Not interchangeable

Education, engineering certifications (such as Autodesk certification), professional licensure (U.S. professional engineer PE: the O*NET certification page lists the "fundamentals of engineering examination, mechanical" and the "control systems engineering professional examination" administered by the National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying), institutional design review authorization, and product market access approval are different statuses: education does not bring licensure, and certification does not mean you can independently sign design or compliance conclusions or conduct testing and calibration in any setting.

Check at least six items before starting: the occupational definition and the employer entity (O*NET 17-2141.02 is a U.S. definition, and its wage and employment data are taken from the same family 17-2141.00; on the mainland China side the position and the employer must be identified); education and major direction; institutional design review and change control authorization; the scope of authorization for testing and calibration work; data, intellectual property, and confidentiality requirements; and the pay method (monthly salary, project bonus, or annual performance pay).
Occupational definition

The U.S. side is O*NET 17-2141.02 (Automotive Engineers); this code is a detailed occupation under 17-2141 Mechanical Engineers, and the wages, employment, and industry data shown by O*NET are taken from 17-2141.00 Mechanical Engineers. On the mainland China side you must first identify whether the position belongs to the whole-vehicle and system development department of a vehicle manufacturer, the product development department of a parts manufacturer, a new energy and three-electric system development department, a test and calibration center, or an engineering consulting and technical service company, because different employers differ greatly in development processes, review, and compliance requirements.
Education and major pathways

On the U.S. side a bachelor's degree (mechanical engineering or mechanical engineering technology) predominates, consistent with the education composition of the same family 17-2141.00 (71% bachelor's degree, 14% master's degree, 5% postsecondary certificate); on the mainland China side the main majors are vehicle engineering, mechanical engineering and automation, and power machinery and engineering, with specific education requirements set by the employer.
Authorization to work and work permits

Design reviews, design changes, testing and calibration work, and product market access and type approval must follow institutional processes and the applicable regulations. On the U.S. side every state and the District of Columbia require mechanical engineers who offer services to the public to be licensed (BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook), and the O*NET certification page lists the "fundamentals of engineering examination, mechanical" and the "control systems engineering professional examination" (National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying); on the mainland China side new energy vehicle manufacturers and products are subject to market access management (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology Order No. 39, as amended by Order No. 54). Before starting, verify pre-job training, review and change authorization, and the compliance determination process; this cannot be inferred directly from education or certification.
Equipment and site safety

Testing and calibration work must meet the applicable safety and environmental requirements (electrical and high-voltage, mechanical and rotating equipment, fuel and exhaust, ventilation and fire, personal protection, and emergency response); work on new energy high-voltage systems must follow dedicated procedures. The O*NET work context shows that 70% work indoors in a controlled environment every day, 14% wear routine protective or safety equipment every day, and 48% consider precision extremely important; the GB 7258 revision project additionally proposes that the doors of new energy vehicles should be openable from inside and outside in abnormal situations such as accident power loss, that the power battery location and high-voltage system release emergency rescue requirements should be given in the instructions, and that monitoring and warning requirements for power battery voltage, current, and temperature parameters should be added. This page does not constitute design, test, or field work instructions.
Shifts and working hours

The work context shows that 71% work more than 40 hours per week, 90% have a regular work schedule, 19% face time pressure every day, and 43% consider competition intense; common arrangements include overtime driven by project milestones and prototype and test cycles. When comparing jobs, put the working-hours structure and the overtime and project bonus arrangements into the written terms.
Continuing training and review

New energy and alternative power, computerized automotive applications (long-range telematics, intelligent transportation systems, artificial intelligence, automatic controls), control algorithms, and calibration update quickly (O*NET lists 36 hot technologies, including Python 8%, MATLAB 6%, C++ 3%, C 2%, and SQL 1%, and separately lists 10 shortage skills), requiring ongoing continuing training and maintenance of tool versions and methods; before starting, confirm the training arrangements and the design review, change control, and data review mechanisms.

paragraphs: All six directions are grounded in mathematics, physics, and engineering fundamentals, but the deliverables and responsibility boundaries differ; the same stint of design or project experience cannot be directly converted into another direction's authorization to work, professional licensure, or design review and compliance determination authorization, and this page only compares differences in duties under the published definitions.

The comparison basis is the official occupation description for O*NET 17-2141.02 and the related occupations list shown on the O*NET page, together with the adjacent-occupation relationships flagged in the routing material; an adjacent relationship only indicates that duties are close and does not mean qualifications, licenses, or authorizations are interchangeable.

The table below compares automotive engineers with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: career direction, core work and output, key differences, and which choice fits each preference better.

In the same 17-2141 occupation family, mechanical engineers cover broader mechanical and thermal systems, while automotive engineers narrow the object to vehicles and vehicle systems and take on vehicle safety, emissions, and regulatory compliance.

If you would rather do the design and development of general mechanical and thermal systems, compare mechanical engineers first; if you would rather do the design and development of vehicles and vehicle systems, automotive engineers fit you.
Design and develop mechanical and thermal systems and equipment, with output mainly in the form of design documents and engineering analysis reports.
Automotive engineers and mechanical engineers

Focuses on test preparation, execution, and data collection and usually does not carry design sealing responsibility; automotive engineers focus on design and analysis and take responsibility for design assumptions.
If you would rather do test execution and data collection, compare automotive engineering technicians first; if you would rather do design and analysis, automotive engineers fit you.
Build test benches to specification, conduct tests, and deliver reviewable test data and records.
Automotive engineers and automotive engineering technicians

Focuses on fuel cell systems and their materials and electrochemistry, with a more concentrated field; the vehicle system scope of automotive engineers is broader, covering power, chassis, body, and electronic control.
If you would rather specialize in fuel cell systems, compare fuel cell engineers first; if you would rather do whole-vehicle and multi-system design, automotive engineers fit you.
Design and validate fuel cell systems and their key materials and components, with output mainly in the form of system solutions and validation conclusions.
Automotive engineers and fuel cell engineers

Focuses on the design and analysis of aircraft and related systems and carries airworthiness and higher safety responsibility; automotive engineers focus on vehicle systems and carry vehicle safety and emissions compliance.
If you would rather do aircraft and system design and analysis, compare aerospace engineers first; if you would rather do vehicle and system design, automotive engineers fit you.
Perform design, analysis, and validation of aircraft and systems, with output mainly in the form of design documents and analysis conclusions.
Automotive engineers and aerospace engineers

Focuses on electrical systems, motors, and power electronics and equipment, with the field concentrated in electrical engineering; automotive engineers integrate multiple systems such as mechanical, electrical, and control on a vehicle platform.
If you would rather do electrical system and equipment design, compare electrical engineers first; if you would rather do multi-system integrated vehicle design, automotive engineers fit you.
Design and validate electrical systems and equipment, with output mainly in the form of electrical design documents and validation conclusions.
Automotive engineers and electrical engineers
Focuses on process and efficiency optimization of production and service systems, with people and processes as the object; automotive engineers work on vehicle products and systems.
If you would rather do process and efficiency optimization, compare industrial engineers first; if you would rather do vehicle product and system design, automotive engineers fit you.
Design and improve processes, workstations, and scheduling, with output mainly in the form of process proposals and efficiency metrics.
Automotive engineers and industrial engineers

Conclusion: the basis for choosing a direction is the deliverables and the responsibility boundaries, not whether vehicles or engineering data are involved in all of them; once the direction is set, the education, professional training, licensure or professional title requirements, and position design review and compliance determination authorization requirements of the target direction should be verified item by item.

entries.answer: There are three core categories of tasks: designing or analyzing vehicle systems with computer-aided design technology (covering fields such as aerodynamics, alternative fuels, ergonomics, hybrid power, brakes, transmissions, steering, calibration, safety, or diagnostics), creating alternative design options for vehicle components to improve fuel efficiency, and designing vehicles that use lightweight materials or improve recyclability; conducting or directing system-level automotive testing, performing failure, variation, and root cause analysis, calibrating vehicle systems including control algorithms or other software systems, developing calibration or test methods or tools, building models for algorithm or control function validation, and designing control systems or algorithms for energy management or emissions management or improved operating safety or performance; and developing engineering specifications and cost estimates and production or quality control standards, conducting automotive design reviews, writing and reviewing and maintaining engineering documentation, preparing or presenting technical and project status reports, and coordinating with functions such as procurement, maintenance, and quality control. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET 17-2141.02, whose official duties are to use computer-aided design technology to develop new or improved designs for vehicle structural members, engines, transmissions, or other vehicle systems and to direct the building, modification, or testing of vehicles or components.
entries.question: What do automotive engineers do every day?

entries.answer: Mainly misjudgment in vehicle safety-related design or calibration, risks related to new energy high-voltage systems and power battery thermal runaway, emissions and environmental compliance risk, unreliable conclusions from insufficient design assumptions and validation, confidentiality risk from external sharing of design data and technical materials, and untraceable design changes and records. The controls are executing to the applicable standards, confirming assumptions and criteria and test conditions first, and recording honestly and accepting review. This page does not provide design, test, or field work instructions.
entries.question: What risks should I watch for in advance in this job?

entries.answer: The more explanatory signals are: being able to complete design, analysis, and validation to standard and record assumptions and limitations honestly, being able to turn requirements into verifiable criteria and judge whether the data support the conclusions, and stopping and escalating when the basis is unclear or the work is beyond authorization; "liking cars" or "being able to use one software product" alone cannot settle it. The Holland interest code is RIC (Realistic + Investigative + Conventional), and a consistent interest only indicates that the direction is close.
entries.question: How do I judge whether I am suited to being an automotive engineer?

entries.answer: AI and automation can change parametric modeling and design exploration, simulation and optimization computation, automatic data processing and anomaly marking, calibration data processing and parameter fitting, and draft document and report generation; but there is no official evidence that they will replace requirement and constraint confirmation, design assumption and criteria determination, failure and root cause judgment, and safety-related calibration and compliance conclusions as a whole. The official materials also do not give an automation substitution rate or a job disappearance year for this occupation.
entries.question: Which tasks will AI change?

entries.answer: Confirmation of requirements and constraints and criteria, design assumptions and the validation plan, verification of models and boundary conditions, test and calibration conditions and data authenticity, failure and root cause judgment, and safety-related design and compliance conclusions must all be undertaken by the individual together with authorized personnel according to institutional processes; tool output must first be marked as reference and can only enter formal design and compliance documents after verification and test validation and design review.
entries.question: Which steps must retain manual review?

entries.answer: U.S. side: O*NET lists 17-2141.02 as Job Zone Four (SVP 7.0 to <8.0), and among the education levels published on the page 71% is requiring a bachelor's degree, 14% is requiring a master's degree, and 5% is requiring a postsecondary certificate; the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook lists the typical entry-level education for this occupation family as a bachelor's degree (mechanical engineering or mechanical engineering technology), with no related work experience and no on-the-job training required, and also notes that every state and the District of Columbia require mechanical engineers who offer services to the public to be licensed; the O*NET certification page lists the NCEES "fundamentals of engineering examination, mechanical" and "control systems engineering professional examination" and Autodesk certification. Mainland China side: this occupation is not listed separately in the classification and falls under the engineering technician intermediate class; new energy vehicle manufacturers and products are subject to market access management, and products must be tested as qualified by a nationally recognized testing agency and meet the safety technical conditions. Education, certification, practice or professional title, institutional design review authorization, and product market access permits cannot substitute for one another.
entries.question: What qualifications must be verified to enter this occupation?

entries.answer: Relatively lower than technician and mechanic positions. The O*NET work context shows that 57% sit more than half the time, 70% stand less than half the time, 84% walk or run less than half the time, 70% work indoors in a controlled environment every day, and 14% wear routine protective or safety equipment every day. However, the testing, calibration, and prototype stages may still involve on-site work and high-voltage system protection requirements; the core abilities are engineering analysis and design judgment and documentation and collaboration.
entries.question: Does this job have high physical demands?

entries.answer: The work context shows that 71% work more than 40 hours per week, 90% have a regular work schedule, 100% use email every day, 75% need face-to-face discussions every day, 70% talk on the telephone every day, and 43% consider competition intense; common arrangements include overtime driven by project milestones and prototype and test cycles. When comparing jobs, put the working-hours structure, the overtime and project bonus arrangements, test and high-voltage work conditions, and data confidentiality requirements into the written terms.
entries.question: What are the working hours and the way of working like?

entries.answer: The official employment projection is about 293,100 people employed in 2024 for the same family occupation, with 2024—2034 growth described as "much faster than average (7% or higher)" and about 18,100 openings per year; the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook gives, for 2025—2035, about 298,500 people employed in the same family occupation, 11% growth, a net gain of about 33,500 jobs, and about 17,800 openings per year, mostly from replacement needs. On the mainland China industry side, Ministry of Industry and Information Technology data show that in 2025 the share of new energy vehicle sales in new vehicle sales reached 47.9%. A projection is not an individual hiring probability. For transitions you can compare directions such as mechanical engineers, automotive engineering technicians, fuel cell engineers, aerospace engineers, electrical engineers, industrial engineers, validation engineers, and manufacturing engineers, but qualifications and authorizations must be verified item by item.
